edits.content: - An implicit universal generalization even without "all"/"every" (e.g. "Students who study pass" = "all students who study pass") — this applies specifically to sentences with a restrictive relative clause or class-defining subject ("X who/that do Y") generalizing over members of a class. It does NOT apply to simple conditional-style claims phrased with generic subjects, including "is necessary/sufficient for", "if...then", "unless", etc. (e.g. "A passing grade is sufficient for graduation eligibility" is a plain conditional — translate it as P→Q using Step 3's necessary/sufficient rules, not as INVALID).
